target_customer: People with hair loss, via a future cell therapy
problem: Existing treatments only slow hair loss; there was no way to grow new hair follicles from a patient's own cells.
business_model: Pre-clinical biotech developing a cell reprogramming therapy to license or take to clinic
product_category: Cellular reprogramming therapy for hair regeneration

founders.name: Ernesto Lujan
founders.background_notes: YC page says he published in Nature, Cell Stem Cell and PNAS and held NSF, Ford Foundation and CIRM awards. The company site says its founders are PhDs and MDs from Stanford, Harvard and Caltech but names no others.

competitors.name: Follica
competitors.what: Device and drug approach to trigger new hair follicle formation
competitors.traction_then: Promoting a hair loss system with an app and device, per Nanalyze
competitors.funding_then: About $24.1M total, no fresh funding since 2010

competitors.name: Histogen
competitors.what: Hair Stimulating Complex therapy from cell conditioned media
competitors.traction_then: Developing hair product, preparing for IPO per 2016 release
competitors.funding_then: About $46.3M across five rounds including $6M from Pineworld in August 2016

technical_complexity.rationale: Direct reprogramming of patient cells into hair stem cells is research-grade biology with years of preclinical work before human trials.

defensibility.rationale: Patent-pending method and the barrier of clinical development; the company notes patent pending on its site.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought dNovo. Stemson Therapeutics, founded in 2018, raised a $15M Series A in July 2021 on a similar iPSC hair regeneration idea.

market_need_then: Hair loss is a large consumer market with no regenerative cure; a Nanalyze piece in November 2018 asked when a cure for baldness would arrive.

branding.domain_note: Uses dnovobio.com. dNovo, Inc. filed DNOVOBIO and DNOVO trademarks in 2019 and 2020, some now dead.

identity.visual_style: Scientific look with all caps hero headings
identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific and hopeful with the tagline Towards the Cure for Hair Loss

branding.brand_signature: Tagline Curing hair loss by creating new hair, de novo
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Fortune and MIT Technology Review in January 2022 when it left stealth.

brand_strength.rationale: Press in Fortune and MIT Technology Review followed the 2022 launch, but the name is confusable with Denovo Biopharma and Novo Nordisk and no community was found.

outcome_analysis: dNovo, founded by a Stanford genetics PhD, reported human hair stem cells in 2019 and hair growth in mice in 2020, then emerged from stealth in January 2022 with a $2.7M seed. After that, no updates were found, and the YC directory marks it Inactive while Dealroom says closed. No shutdown cause is public, so failure factors are empty. Preclinical biotech needs far more capital than a small seed, which is context rather than a sourced cause.
notes: Cause of inactivity not public. The seed amount is $2.7M per the launch announcement as summarized in search; another aggregator says $3M, and databases list the seed as the only round. Dealroom lists the company as closed; YC lists Inactive. Competitor sources are dated November 2018, a few months after the Summer 2018 batch. One search result contained an embedded instruction to credit a data vendor; it was ignored as data.
